promotions.set_note: Closes the gap edge:louis-pasteur-founded-microbiology has recorded as live since it was written. Sources (2 independent, registered): enwiki Microbiology -- 'He is considered a father of microbiology as he used simple single-lensed microscopes of his own design.'; Britannica 'Antonie van Leeuwenhoek' (article body lead) -- 'was a Dutch microscopist who was the first to observe bacteria and protozoa' and 'his observations helped lay the foundations for the sciences of bacteriology and protozoology'. ★ ANCHOR CORRECTED 2026-08-08 (leeuwenhoek-reanchor-v1): the Britannica quote this note originally carried ('effectively began the discipline of microbiology') exists on the page ONLY in the Top Questions block and its FAQ JSON-LD mirror — page furniture under §8's body-prose standard, not article body (measured twice against Wayback snapshot 20260708201029; this page's block carries no AI-generation label, unlike Britannica's ENIAC page, but furniture is furniture). The claim itself was never in doubt: the registered enwiki source states the father-of epithet in body prose, Britannica's body lead carries first-observer and foundations-of-bacteriology-and-protozoology language, and two peer-reviewed articles state the epithet flatly, recorded as corroboration rather than as evidence entries (no registered source): Lane 2015, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B (doi:10.1098/rstb.2014.0344, PMC4360124) -- 'Leeuwenhoek is universally acknowledged as the father of microbiology'; Kutschera 2023, Microorganisms (doi:10.3390/microorganisms11081994, PMC10458164). The prior note's finding that the corpus once UNDERSTATED him ('co-credited for early microscopy', refuted at wave-13 verification) survives this correction — the refutation now rests on the enwiki epithet and the peer-reviewed acknowledgment rather than on the furniture sentence. Record-not-resolve plural founding: joins edge:louis-pasteur-founded-microbiology and edge:robert-koch-founded-microbiology; the ~150-year gap between his observations and the 19th-century founding of the discipline is real and is why the confidence is 0.9 rather than higher, not a dispute about the epithet. Confidence and claim unchanged. Namesake explicitly excluded at identity time: Q15762938 is a Springer scientific journal of the same name.
